title: The best suites sell a door, not a room.
subtitle: Square footage is the easiest thing to price and the least likely to change your week.

text: Some suite tiers add space. Some add standing.
sub: One gives you a larger sitting room you will use twice. The other changes how the ship treats you from the moment you reach the terminal until the morning you leave it.

items.head: Buy the lowest access tier
items.body: The entry rung of the privileged block carries most of the privilege at the smallest premium.

items.head: Ignore the corner showpiece
items.body: The photographed suite is priced as a trophy. The one beside it is quieter and far less dear.

items.head: Check what the tier includes
items.body: On inclusive fares much of the suite benefit is already yours. Then you are only buying the room.

quote: On a good ship the butler is worth more than the extra forty feet, and costs less to obtain.

text: Ask what the tier gets you *off* the ship, not just inside it.
sub: Priority tender, a reserved table on a full sea day, a name who fixes things in the moment. Those alter a voyage. A second wardrobe does not, at any price per night.

title: Send this to whoever is weighing up a suite.
body: Or send me the two categories you're deciding between. I'll tell you which one buys something you'll notice, and which is charging you for floor area.
